subject.title: memory_search: chokidar file watcher silently stops delivering events, index goes stale

question: Should this issue be solved by making periodic memory sync an opt-out default fallback, by keeping `intervalMinutes` defaulted to `0` and adding narrower watcher health/recovery, or by requiring operators to configure the fallback manually?
rationale: The source-level bug is clear, but the open candidate fix changes default background indexing behavior, which can affect upgrade cost and provider usage; that default policy needs maintainer intent before merge.

options.title: Land opt-out periodic fallback
options.body: Resolve the linked PR conflicts, keep explicit `intervalMinutes: 0` as opt-out, and ship the dirty-aware interval fallback with docs and upgrade proof.

options.title: Keep default 0 and repair watcher liveness
options.body: Avoid new background work for existing users, but require a robust watcher health/recovery implementation that still catches silent missed events.

options.title: Document manual fallback only
options.body: Leave runtime defaults unchanged and point users to `intervalMinutes`, but this would not protect default users from the reported stale-index failure.

recommendation.title: Land opt-out periodic fallback
recommendation.body: Resolve the linked PR conflicts, keep explicit `intervalMinutes: 0` as opt-out, and ship the dirty-aware interval fallback with docs and upgrade proof.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest current-main memory search and memory-engine history and is best positioned to decide the default/background-work policy.
